## Birthweight Z-Score and Cell Proportions

Here we are performing several models to evaluate the association between birthweight z-score and placental cell proportions in the CANDLE and PATHWAYS GAPPS cohorts (N=1009). We are modelling this with several methods: Composition Model, Bootstrapped Composition Model, and Beta Regressions.

### Upload Data and Load Packages
```{r data and packages}
#Load Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(compositions)
library(robCompositions)
library(data.table)
library(parallel)
library(betareg)
library(foreach)
library(DirichletReg)
library(marginaleffects)

#Load Data
load("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/ImputedCellProportions_withcollapse_CANDLEGAPPS_N1009_111825.RData")
load("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/CovariateData/FilteredCovariates_CANDLEGAPPS_111825.RData")
percent_detected <-read.csv("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/CellTypes_PercentDetected_AfterCollapse_N1009_CANDLEGAPPS_111825.csv")
load("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/composition_order_aftercollapse_111825.RData")
```

### Prepare Data and Check Covariates
```{r prep data and check covariates}
# add cell type data to covariate data.
data = ciber_cells_impute_res %>%  
  inner_join(CANDLE_GAPPS_FinalCovars)
#Check Data types
summary(data)
#All variables look good- but ethnicity, fetal sex, and parity have empty factor levels
data$Ethnicity <- factor(data$Ethnicity, levels=c("0", "1"))
data$FetalSex <- factor(data$FetalSex, levels=c("F", "M"))
data$Parity <- factor(data$Parity, levels=c("0", "1"))
data$RaceCollapsed <- factor(data$RaceCollapsed, levels=c("1", "2", "3", "6", "7"))
data$Batch <- factor(data$Batch, levels=c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7"))
summary(data)


composition_order_underscores <-gsub(" ", "_", composition_order)
```

### Birthweight and Cell Proportions- Composition Models
These models are evaluating the association between Birthweight and Cell Proportions (relative proportion), but do not give p-values for individual cell types. 

```{r BW and cell prop}
# reduce our cell_types variable to only include retained cell types
cell_types <- colnames(ciber_cells_impute_res)[colnames(ciber_cells_impute_res) != "pathways_id"]

# acomp is relative composition method, now all rows should sum to 1
outcome <- compositions::acomp(ciber_cells_impute_res[,cell_types])
rowSums(outcome)

# ilr:() is the Isometric log ratio transformation
comp_mod <- lm(ilr(outcome) ~ Age + BMI + EducationCollapsed  + RaceCollapsed + Ethnicity + FetalSex + Parity + LaborType + DeliveryMethod + SmokingComposite + Alcohol + Batch + bw_z, data=data)

# extract coefficients in inverse-ILR scale
compositions::ilrInv(coef(comp_mod), orig=outcome)

# extract pvalue associated with gestational week
anova(comp_mod)['bw_z',6] ## Significant association!

## NOTE: One of the limitations of the 'compositions' package is that the 
##       p-value calculation is only correct for the last covariate in the 
##       model formula.  
##       In this example, the p-value for "bw_z" is correct, but not 
##       for infant sex. In order to calculate the correct p-value for "sex", 
##       you need to refit the same model with "sex" at the end of the formula: 
##      --> "ilr(outcome) ~ gestation_wk + sex"
## Reference: for further details, see Section 5.3.5 of Van den Boogaart,
##            Tolsana and Delgado (2013).

# perturbation applied to the composition if X increases one unit 
# ilrINV brings the coefs back to the original scale. Demonstrations of this transformation from the 
# source above (authors of the compositions package)
ga_coef <- compositions::ilrInv(coef(comp_mod), orig=outcome)['bw_z',]
# taking the mean of all participant compositions with this perturbation applied
# in a relative composition manner (cell types sum to 1 even after taking mean)
exp_ccomp <- mean(compositions::acomp(ga_coef) + outcome)
exp_ccomp

sum(ga_coef)
#rowSums(outcome)
sum(exp_ccomp)

# calculate expected change in cell proportions for 1 unit increase in bw-zscore
# this is the difference between the mean of all participants with the 
# beta coefficient change (perturbation) applied from above, and the mean of the actual composition 
# of all participants. See https://clinicalepigeneticsjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13148-023-01601-x for similar method 
exp_change <- as.numeric(exp_ccomp) - as.numeric(mean(outcome))
names(exp_change) <- names(outcome)
exp_change


# can multiple each one by 100 for a percent change
exp_change_percent <- exp_change *100
exp_change_percent

# also get relative effect (ratio). Easier to compare with beta regression effect estimates
exp_change_relative <- as.numeric(exp_ccomp) / as.numeric(mean(outcome))
names(exp_change_relative) <- names(outcome)
exp_change_relative

#Combine Expected Change to one dataframe

ExpChange_DF <- data.frame(exp_change,exp_change_percent, exp_change_relative)

#write.csv(ExpChange_DF, "/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Results/BW_ZScore/Birthweight_CompModel_ExpectedChange_020926.csv")

```

### Birthweight and Cell Proporstions- Bootstrapping
These models evaluate birthweight and cell proprotions and have p-values for each individual cell type.
```{r BW and cell prop - bootstrapping}
################################################################################
# (3) Bootstrap approach to estimate confidence intervals and corrected p-value
#     for the effect of increasing birthweight Z-score by 1 unit on placenta cell
#     type composition.
################################################################################
nboot = 1000 # number of bootstrap repetitions
no_cores = detectCores() - 1 # number of computer cores to use for parallel loop 
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores) # create parallel backend
clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 123) # Set seed for reproducibility
clusterEvalQ(cl, {
  library(compositions)
  library(data.table)
  library(parallel)
})

clusterExport(cl, varlist = c("nboot","data","cell_types"))

# parallel loop that runs compositional regressions for each bootstrap data set and stores results
tmp = parLapplyLB(cl,1:nboot,function(b){
  
  # sample from original data with replacement
  rep_idx <- sample(x=1:nrow(data), size=nrow(data), replace=T)
  boot_data <- data[rep_idx,]
  
  # perform analysis on bootstrap data and save estimates
  outcome_b = acomp(boot_data[,cell_types]) # this is the cell types, like outcome in the above example, but only for this bootstrapped sample

  # fit compositional model on current bootstrap data
  comp_mod_b <- lm(ilr(outcome_b) ~ Age + BMI + EducationCollapsed  + RaceCollapsed + Ethnicity + FetalSex + Parity + LaborType + DeliveryMethod + SmokingComposite + Alcohol + Batch + bw_z, data=boot_data)
  
  # extract F statistic (only used for the overal p-value)
  Fstat_b = anova(comp_mod_b)['bw_z', 3]
  
  # extract exposure coefficient in inverse ILR scale
  # the reason we are bootstrapping is to get 95% CIs for these, each individual cell types effect on BW Z-Score.
  # a single composition model only gives you p values for the effect of the entire composition 
  #coef_b <- ilrInv(coef(comp_mod_b), orig=outcome_b)['bw_z',] This is the previous version that is not quite right for bootstrap since hte outcome_b can change in each bootstrap iteration
  
  basis <- ilrBase(outcome_b)
coef_b <- ilrInv(coef(comp_mod_b), V = basis)['bw_z',]
  
  # calculate the expected cell composition after 1 unit increase in exposure
  # for each participant we are adding the coef for a 1 week increase to their actual cell type.
  # the addition is in a relative composition way, not Euclidean space. Adding two acomp class objects, each participants composition will still sum to one.
  exp_outcome = mean(acomp(coef_b) + outcome_b)
  
  # expected change in cell composition after 1 unit increase in exposure (original scale)
  exp_outcome_change = as.numeric(exp_outcome) - as.numeric(mean(outcome_b))
  
  ## we also need to boostrap relative percent chance, rather than absolute changes to compare with beta regression
  # because beta regression uses logit link and is multiplicative
  exp_outcome_relative_change = as.numeric(exp_outcome) / as.numeric(mean(outcome_b))
  
  # store results
  dt <- data.table(t(exp_outcome_change), 
                   Fstat = Fstat_b)

  dt.relative = data.table(t(exp_outcome_relative_change), 
                   Fstat = Fstat_b)
  res = list(dt=dt,dt.relative=dt.relative)
})
stopCluster(cl) # stop parallel backend


# Extract dt (absolute changes) from all bootstrap iterations
bootstrap_results <- rbindlist(lapply(tmp, function(x) x$dt))
colnames(bootstrap_results)[1:length(cell_types)] <- cell_types

# calculate 95% bootstrap Confidence intervals.
# -20 removed the Fstat col from this
boot_CIs <- as.data.frame(apply(bootstrap_results[,-20], 2, 
                              quantile, probs=c(0.025,0.975)))

# get df for p values
get_df = summary(comp_mod)$"Response Y1"$fstatistic
get_df["numdf"]
get_df["dendf"]
# calculate bootstrap corrected p-value using the median F-statistic 
# p value for the entire compositional effect.
boot_pvalue <- pf(median(bootstrap_results$Fstat), get_df["numdf"], get_df["dendf"], lower.tail=F)
print(boot_pvalue)

# original estimate from exp_change. This is the estimate we are bootstrapping 95% CIs around
exp_change_original = as.data.frame(exp_change)
exp_change_original$cell_type <- rownames(exp_change_original)
boot_CIs = t(boot_CIs) %>% as.data.frame()
boot_CIs$cell_type <- rownames(boot_CIs)

final_res = exp_change_original %>% left_join(boot_CIs) %>% 
  mutate(overall_composition_p_value=boot_pvalue) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(conf.low = "2.5%",
                conf.high = "97.5%")%>% 
  mutate(exp_change = exp_change*100, # multiply by 100 to get % instead of proportion
         conf.low = conf.low*100,
         conf.high= conf.high*100) %>% 
    mutate(estimate_with_ci = paste0(
    round(exp_change, 3), " [", round(conf.low, 3), " to ", round(conf.high, 3), "]")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(cell_type, exp_change, conf.low, conf.high, estimate_with_ci, overall_composition_p_value)%>%
  mutate(significant = if_else(
    sign(exp_change) == sign(conf.low) & sign(exp_change) == sign(conf.high),  # Check if all signs are the same to evaluate significance
    "yes", 
    "no"
  ))

final_res=final_res%>%
  mutate(cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = composition_order_underscores)) %>%
  arrange(cell_type)

#write_csv(final_res, "/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Results/BW_ZScore/Birthweight_CellProportions_BootstrapResults_N1009_020926.csv")

###
#### same thing but for multiplicative changes
####

# Extract dt (relative changes) from all bootstrap iterations
bootstrap_results <- rbindlist(lapply(tmp, function(x) x$dt.relative))
colnames(bootstrap_results)[1:length(cell_types)] <- cell_types
colnames(bootstrap_results)[length(cell_types) + 1] <- "Fstat"

# calculate 95% bootstrap Confidence intervals.
boot_CIs <- as.data.frame(apply(bootstrap_results, 2, 
                              quantile, probs=c(0.025,0.975)))

# get df for p values (not really needed, same p-value as above)
get_df = summary(comp_mod)$"Response Y1"$fstatistic
get_df["numdf"]
get_df["dendf"]

exp_change_original = as.data.frame(exp_change_relative)
exp_change_original$cell_type <- rownames(exp_change_original)
boot_CIs = t(boot_CIs) %>% as.data.frame()
boot_CIs$cell_type <- rownames(boot_CIs)

final_res_relative = exp_change_original %>% left_join(boot_CIs) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(conf.low = "2.5%",
                conf.high = "97.5%")%>%  
    mutate(estimate_with_ci = paste0(
    round(exp_change_relative, 3), " [", round(conf.low, 3), " to ", round(conf.high, 3), "]")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(cell_type, exp_change_relative, conf.low, conf.high, estimate_with_ci)%>%
  mutate(significant = if_else(
    (exp_change_relative > 1 & conf.low > 1 & conf.high > 1) | (exp_change_relative < 1 & conf.low < 1 & conf.high < 1), 
    "yes", 
    "no"))
final_res_relative=final_res_relative%>%
  mutate(cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = composition_order_underscores)) %>%
  arrange(cell_type)


#write_csv(final_res_relative, "/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Results/BW_ZScore/Birthweight_CellProportions_BootstrapResults_Multiplicative_N1009_020926.csv")
```

### Birthweight and Cell Proportions- Beta Regression
The Beta regressions model each cell type 1 at a time (without accounting for other cell types). The outcome is a proportion between 0-1. 
```{r BW Beta regressions}

# for cell types with low detection and generally low proportions, we get this error:
# Error in chol.default(K) : the leading minor of order 2 is not positive
# this loop allows errors and reports them in the final results

betareg_bw <- foreach(i = cell_types, .combine = "rbind") %do% {
  result <- tryCatch({
    b1 <- betareg(paste0(i,  "~ bw_z +  Age + BMI + EducationCollapsed +  RaceCollapsed + Ethnicity + FetalSex + Parity + LaborType + DeliveryMethod + SmokingComposite + Alcohol + Batch"), 
                  data = data)
    
    broom::tidy(b1, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
      mutate(estimate = exp(estimate),
             conf.low = exp(conf.low),
             conf.high = exp(conf.high)) %>% 
      mutate(estimate_with_ci = paste0(
        round(estimate, 3), " [", round(conf.low, 3), " to ", round(conf.high, 3), "]")) %>% 
      filter(term == "bw_z") %>% 
      mutate(significant = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "yes", "no")) %>%
      mutate(cell_type = i) %>% 
      dplyr::select(cell_type, term, estimate, std.error, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, estimate_with_ci, significant)
  }, error = function(e) {
    data.frame(
      cell_type = i,
      term = "bw_z",
      estimate = "Error",
      std.error = "Error",
      p.value = "Error",
      conf.low = "Error",
      conf.high = "Error",
      estimate_with_ci = "Error",
      significant = "Error"
    )
  })
  
  return(result)
}

### Marginal Effects Code
# list of the cell types where the beta regression did not fail
cell_types2 = betareg_bw %>% filter(estimate != "Error") %>% pull(cell_type)

ame_df <- foreach(i = cell_types2, .combine = "rbind") %do% {

  formula_i <- as.formula(
    paste0(i,  "~ bw_z +  Age + BMI + EducationCollapsed +  RaceCollapsed + Ethnicity + FetalSex + Parity + LaborType + DeliveryMethod + SmokingComposite + Alcohol + Batch")
    )
  
  model <- betareg(formula_i, data = data)
  # avg_slopes used for 1 unit increase in continuous exposure. avg_comparisons used for binary exposure variable like PTB
  avg_slopes(
    model,
    variables = "bw_z",
    newdata = data,
    type = "response"
  ) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0("ame_", .x)) %>%
    mutate(cell_type = i)
}

 # SCALE BY 100 HERE: transforms proportion (0.01) to percentage points (1.0)
ame_df <- ame_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
      ame_estimate_percent = ame_estimate * 100,
      ame_conf.low_percent = ame_conf.low * 100,
      ame_conf.high_percent = ame_conf.high * 100
    )


betareg_bw = betareg_bw%>%
  left_join(ame_df) %>% 
  mutate(cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = composition_order_underscores)) %>%
  arrange(cell_type) %>% left_join(percent_detected)

betareg_bw

```

### Compare across Regression Types
```{r compare}
#Pull Sig Cell Types
Sig_Boot <- final_res %>%
  dplyr::filter(significant=="yes") %>%
  dplyr::select(cell_type, exp_change, conf.low, conf.high)
Sig_Boot$RegressionType <- c("Bootstrap Composition")
colnames(Sig_Boot) <- c("CellType", "Estimate", "CI_Low", "CI_High", "RegressionType")

Sig_Beta <- betareg_bw %>%
  dplyr::filter(significant=="yes") %>%
  dplyr::select(cell_type, ame_estimate_percent, ame_conf.low_percent, ame_conf.high_percent)
Sig_Beta$RegressionType <- c("Beta Regression")
colnames(Sig_Beta) <- c("CellType", "Estimate", "CI_Low", "CI_High", "RegressionType")


# Combine
CombinedResults <- rbind(Sig_Boot, Sig_Beta)

#Fix Formatting of Cell Types
CombinedResults$CellType <- gsub("_", " ", CombinedResults$CellType)
CombinedResults$CellType <- str_to_title(CombinedResults$CellType)

#Fix Estimate Data Class
class(CombinedResults$Estimate)
CombinedResults$Estimate <- as.numeric(CombinedResults$Estimate)
class(CombinedResults$Estimate)

# Plot for easy visualization
ggplot(CombinedResults, aes(x=RegressionType, y=CellType, fill=Estimate)) +
  geom_point(shape=21, size=4) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="#0080A2", mid="white", high="#EC7625", midpoint=0) + 
  ggtitle("Birthweight- ZScores")
```
